evidence: The 2012-10-25 homepage capture is titled 'Mayor Miguel Pulido 2012' and has Bio, Ballot Statement, Endorsements and Donate links. The CDX index for Sep-Nov 2012 lists campaign posts such as 'campaign-reception-for-santa-ana-mayor-miguel-pulido-set-for-oct-4' (2012-09-29), 'u-s-senator-dianne-feinstein-endorses-santa-ana-mayor-miguel-pulido' (2012-11-01) and 'mayor-pulido-thanks-his-supporters-for-their-hard-work-on-his-campaign' (2012-11-04). Many posts copy city press releases, but the site is the 2012 re-election campaign site of the sitting mayor.

The 2013 captures in the input still show the 2011 victory letter, but the site was updated for 2014: the CDX index shows new assets stamped ?1399650039 (2014-05-09, one day before the election), including a new banner and logo. The 2014-05-17 homepage capture (+7 days) is a re-election letter: 'the people of Irving chose to elect me Mayor in 2011' and 'I am asking for your vote and your support so we can continue our fiscally responsible management'. The text concerns the May 2014 race.

The 2013-04-26 issues page (-18 days) has the page title 'Every Day, A Better Jersey City - Reelect Mayor Jerramiah Healy 2013' and describes Healy's record as mayor since 2004. The endorsements page in the input quotes Codey 'lending my support to his re-election as Mayor of Jersey City'. Nothing indicates a different person; Jerramiah Healy was the incumbent who lost to Fulop in May 2013.

The site is Pulido's committee site ('Paid for by Pulido for Mayor, Campaign ID#941-669', 2016-10-19 homepage) and was reused across 2012, 2014 and 2016. It shows activity during the 2016 race: a new post 'Mayor Pulido runs in his third DTSA 5K Run' (published 2016-09-17, captured 2016-09-27), a 'Click below to donate to Mayor Pulido's campaign' widget, and a pingback from 'Santa Ana 2016 General Election Voter Guide' on the Bio page. Weak case: the bio still says 'Term Expires: November 2012' and no page names the 2016 election explicitly.

The 2024-09-10 homepage (-56 days) reads 'NOMINEE FOR BALTIMORE CITY MAYOR', 'Pastor Shannon Wright to Accept Republican Nomination for Mayor of Baltimore City' and 'vote Wright for Baltimore!', with a Donate form. The 2020 material sits under a separate 'MEDIA FROM 2020' menu item, and the May 2024 capture has an 'After 2020' menu. The site was updated and in use for the 2024 race, in which she was the Republican nominee.
